title: Imaging Nuclear Pore Complexes in Zebrafish Embryo Nuclei by FESEM
author: Shen, Meng

steps.title: Load nuclei onto silicon chip
steps.instruction: Spread nuclei onto a silicon chip using an improvised centrifugation holder and low‑speed spin.

substeps.instruction: Discard the supernatant from the crude nuclei pellet.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 100 µL PBS containing 10 % glycerol.
Transfer the suspension to 900 µL PBS + 10 % glycerol placed inside the improvised centrifugation holder (Fig. 2C).
Insert the holder into a standard 50‑mL tube that is densely packed with facial tissues to a suitable level (Fig. 2D).
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 10 min at 4 °C in a swing‑bucket rotor (e.g., Eppendorf 5810 R).

steps.title: Pre‑fix nuclei on silicon chip
steps.instruction: Wash the chip and fix attached nuclei with paraformaldehyde‑glutaraldehyde solution.

substeps.instruction: Using high‑precision tweezers, transfer the silicon chip into a well of a 48‑well plate containing 1 mL PBS for washing; keep the nuclei‑facing side upward and avoid drying.
Move the chip to a second well containing 2 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) + 2 % glutaraldehyde (GA) solution.
Fix for 30 min at room temperature, or optionally overnight (8–16 h) at 4 °C in the dark.

steps.title: Post‑fix nuclei on silicon chip
steps.instruction: Wash, osmium‑tetroxide post‑fix, and rinse the nuclei on the chip.

substeps.instruction: Wash the chip three times in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer (prepared by mixing equal volumes of 0.2 M cacodylate buffer and ddH₂O) for 2 min each.
Post‑fix in freshly prepared 1 % OsO₄ in 0.1 M cacodylate buffer for 10 min at room temperature in the dark (mix equal volumes of 2 % OsO₄ and 0.2 M cacodylate buffer just before use).
Transfer the chip to a new 48‑well plate filled with filtered (0.22 µm) ddH₂O and wash for 2 min.
Repeat the ddH₂O wash two additional times, 2 min each.

steps.title: Dehydrate and critical point dry
steps.instruction: Gradually replace water with ethanol and dry the chip by CO₂ critical‑point drying.

substeps.instruction: Dehydrate through a graded ethanol series: 30 %, 50 %, 70 %, 90 %, and 95 % (each for 3 min, repeat each step twice).
Transfer the chip to 100 % ethanol for six consecutive 3 min immersions. Samples may be stored in 100 % ethanol overnight if needed.
Place the chip in a critical‑point‑drying apparatus (e.g., Leica EM CPD 300) filled with ethanol.

Exchange the ethanol with high‑purity liquid CO₂ twelve times to ensure complete fluid exchange, then raise temperature and pressure to CO₂’s critical point (31 °C, 74 bar) to convert CO₂ to gas and dry the specimen.

steps.title: Sputter coat and acquire FESEM images
steps.instruction: Apply a conductive metal layer and image the nuclei by field‑emission scanning electron microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Mount the silicon chip onto an aluminum stub using a carbon‑adhesive tab and place it in a sputter‑coater.
Coat the specimen with a 10‑nm thick layer of gold (alternatives: 3‑nm Cr or 2‑nm Ir, but gold gave better conductivity for zebrafish nuclei).
Image the nuclear pore complexes on a FESEM instrument (e.g., FEI Helios NanoLab G3 UC) following appropriate training or technician assistance.

steps.title: Purify nuclei via sucrose centrifugation (optional)
steps.instruction: Further purify nuclei from the crude pellet using a hypertonic sucrose buffer and high‑speed ultracentrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Discard the residual supernatant, leaving as little liquid as possible.
Add 500 µL hypertonic sucrose buffer to the pellet and gently pipette up and down with a 200‑µL tip to resuspend.
Transfer the suspension to the cylinder of a Dounce homogenizer.
Homogenize on ice with the loose (A) pestle for 8–10 up‑and‑down strokes.
Move the homogenate to a 1.5 mL polypropylene ultracentrifuge tube (Beckman 357448) using a 200‑µL pipette (avoid standard 1.5‑mL EP tubes).
Centrifuge at 80 000 × g for 80 min at 4 °C.
Aspirate the supernatant as completely as possible without disturbing the invisible nuclei pellet at the tube bottom.

Resuspend the pellet in 205 µL PBS (no Triton X‑100) with a 200‑µL tip and transfer to a fresh 1.5 mL EP tube. (Optional: add 0.5 % Triton X‑100 to remove the nuclear envelope, noting increased aggregation.)

steps.title: Collect and store purified nuclei (optional)
steps.instruction: Pellet the nuclei, remove excess buffer, and freeze for later use.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the 200 µL suspension at 800 × g for 10 min at 4 °C to pellet the nuclei.
Discard the supernatant and gently aspirate remaining PBS without touching the pellet.
Snap‑freeze the pellet in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C for up to 1 month (retain 5 µL of the suspension for counting).

steps.title: Quality check and count nuclei (optional)
steps.instruction: Stain a small aliquot of nuclei and assess integrity by confocal microscopy and hemocytometer counting.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µL PBS to the remaining 5 µL nuclei suspension to bring the volume to 10 µL.
Stain with wheat‑germ agglutinin Alexa 647 (final 5 µg/mL) and DAPI (final 1 µg/mL) for 10 min at room temperature.
Place ~2 µL of the stained suspension in a confocal dish and acquire images (WGA labels FG‑Nups, DAPI labels DNA, bright‑field shows nuclear exposure).
Count nuclei using a hemocytometer, then extrapolate to the total volume.

steps.title: Record storage and perform mass spectrometry (optional)
steps.instruction: Document sample details and analyze nuclei by label‑free LC‑MS/MS.

substeps.instruction: Record the tube location and the estimated number of nuclei; pool multiple tubes if needed to reach ~12 500 nuclei per MS sample.
Proceed with the optimized label‑free mass‑spectrometry workflow.

steps.title: Analyze NPC types with ImageJ
steps.instruction: Open FESEM images in Fiji and prepare for counting.

substeps.instruction: Launch ImageJ Fiji and open the FESEM image file.
Activate the "Cell Counter" plugin via Plugins → Analyze → Cell Counter.

steps.title: Classify and count NPC types
steps.instruction: Define NPC categories and tally each type using the Cell Counter tool.

substeps.instruction: Define the six NPC categories (dimples, stable pores, rosette, star rings, thin rings, mature NPCs) based on size, cytoplasmic ring, and central channel morphology.
Click "Initialize" to start a new counting session.
Use "Remove" to delete any unwanted categories.
Rename each category with "Rename" for clear identification.
Select a category and left‑click on each corresponding NPC in the image to count; repeat for all categories.
Press "Results" and export the count data (e.g., as a CSV file).

steps.title: Statistical analysis of NPC fractions
steps.instruction: Calculate and plot the proportion of each NPC type using Prism.

substeps.instruction: Import the exported count file into Prism’s Data Table.
Choose Analyze → Fraction of Total to compute fractional values for each NPC type.
Create a stacked‑bar graph of the fractions for visual comparison.
